provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program works directly on the visible grid. The background is the most common colour. The panel block is the largest 4-connected non-background component, and its bounding box is cropped. Each panel is located by its distinct colour, as the bounding box of that colour inside the crop. The panel's hole count is the number of 4-connected background components in that box, and those holes are then filled with the panel colour. Loose shapes are the non-background components lying outside the block rectangle. Each one's hole count is the number of 4-connected background components in its bounding box. The shape is stamped centred into the panel with the same count; its cells keep their colour and its holes take the panel colour. Rotations, reflections and palette changes preserve every one of these quantities, so no specialisation by d4 or palette is needed. The repair: any component lying entirely inside the block rectangle is now treated as part of the block, never as a loose shape.
draft_notes.limitations: The program relies on constructor guarantees: a gap of at least 1 cell around every object, distinct panel colours, distinct panel hole counts, and the block being the largest component. The block always has at least about 2*S^2-13 cells, while a shape has at most (S-2)^2. If hole counts were duplicated, which the constructor rejects, the first panel in reading order would win; that is not part of the rule. A background tie would be broken by border frequency, but the density limit prevents such ties. Demonstrations are ignored. No tests were run.
draft_notes.diagnosis: The host counterexample fails on train pair 2. Its panel block is 1x3 panels of side 7 on background 3, and the panel coloured 1 has holes at relative (2,4), (3,3), (4,2), (4,4) and (5,3). The four holes around (4,3) touch it only diagonally to each other but block all four of its orthogonal neighbours. That panel cell (grid (10,5), colour 1) therefore becomes its own 4-connected non-background component, separate from the block. The failed program treated every non-block component as a loose shape. It read this 1x1 island as a shape with 0 holes and stamped it at the centre of the 0-hole panel (colour 4). Because components are processed in reading order, this happened after the real solid shape (colour 7, rows 0-4) had been stamped, so the centre cell came out 1 instead of 7. That is the single mismatch behind [true, false, true, true]. The fix is general, not a special case: components contained in the block's bounding rectangle are part of the block. Loose shapes are always at least 1 cell away from the block, so this never drops a real shape. The island is panel-coloured and sits inside its own panel box, so panel extents, hole counts and filling are unaffected.
draft_notes.constructor_issue: No label inconsistency: the expected output agrees with the stated mechanism. The constructor only stops panel holes from being 4-adjacent. With S>=5 and k>=4, a diamond of 4 diagonally touching holes can isolate a single panel cell as its own 4-connected component. With k<=6 and adjacent holes forbidden, only single-cell islands are possible. This is a legitimate scene feature, not a defect, but host reviewers should know that the archived solver mishandles it in two ways. It splits panels by same-colour components, so the island registers as a spurious 1x1 panel with 0 holes and can overwrite the real 0-hole panel entry. It also treats the island as a loose 0-hole object. No constructor change is proposed (constructor_code null); canonical fixtures are unchanged.

host_review.review: Reviewed visible mechanism and reproduced saved counterexamples. Original fixture calls and labels unchanged. Host fresh audit and complete-episode audit recorded separately.
